paper_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity does the paper report on Penn Treebank for its own proposed model?
sub_questions.answer: The best test perplexity reported for the paper's own model on Penn Treebank is 58.3, achieved by a 4-layer LSTM with 24M parameters.
sub_questions.quote: At 24M, all depths obtain very similar results, reaching 58.3 at depth 4.

sub_questions.q: In which setting is the Penn Treebank test perplexity reported for the paper's own model (single model, with dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning)?
sub_questions.answer: The reported perplexity is for a single model without dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning.
sub_questions.quote: All our results are well below the previous state of the art for models without dynamic evaluation or caching.

sub_questions.q: What baseline test perplexities on Penn Treebank does the paper list for comparison?
sub_questions.answer: The paper lists baseline test perplexities: Medium LSTM 82.7, Large LSTM 78.4, VD LSTM (Press & Wolf) 73.2, VD LSTM (Inan et al., 9M) 73.9, VD LSTM (Inan et al., 28M) 69.0, VD RHN 65.4, NAS (25M) 64.0, NAS (54M) 62.4, and AWD-LSTM 57.3.
sub_questions.quote: Medium LSTM, Zaremba et al. 2014 10M 2 86.2 82.7 ... AWD-LSTM, Merity et al. 2017 † 24M 3 60.0 57.3

sub_questions.q: How does the paper's own model's Penn Treebank test perplexity compare with the baselines the paper lists?
sub_questions.answer: The paper's best model (58.3) outperforms all listed baselines except AWD-LSTM (57.3), which is a parallel work and slightly better.
sub_questions.quote: At 24M, all depths obtain very similar results, reaching 58.3 at depth 4.

sub_questions.q: Does the paper report any Penn Treebank results for its own model with dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning?
sub_questions.answer: No, the paper does not report Penn Treebank results for its own model with dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning.
sub_questions.quote: Our aim is strictly to do better model comparisons for these architectures and we thus refrain from including techniques that are known to push perplexities even lower
